what: The owner's #3 on FastH3 V2: the conditioning set (adaln_t_table + every adaln_proj.linear) swapped between fl2va and FastH3, and the plain base, all on FastH3's contract harness (10/3, its rungs through ManualSigmas, euler, core VSA keep 20% from the first step). The FastH3 endpoint is the followup batch's <scene>__fasth3 row: same graph, prompt, length and seed.
why: FastH3 barely moves the backbone linears and moves every block's modulation about 5% (bench/results/2026-09-26_fasth3_weights.md). Which half carries the few-step ability and the owner's 'too much detail' polish?

checkpoints.swap_fasth3adaln: fl2va backbone, FastH3 conditioning, no VSA gates (core's VSA runs the fine stage only and warns)
checkpoints.swap_baseadaln: FastH3 backbone with its gates, fl2va conditioning
checkpoints.fl2va_contract: the plain base on the same harness, no gates

predictions.S1: fl2va_contract is the floor: under-converged at 8 steps, soft and noisy, visibly worse than FastH3 on every scene.
predictions.S2: swap_fasth3adaln lands closer to FastH3 than to the floor on sharpness and convergence, because the conditioning is where FastH3 moved; it falls short of FastH3 where the missing gates and the small backbone change matter, most on the fast-motion scene.
predictions.S3: swap_baseadaln degrades toward the floor: softer, less converged than FastH3.
predictions.S4: the owner's over-polish on look_anchor travels with the conditioning: present in swap_fasth3adaln, absent from swap_baseadaln.
predictions.falsifier: if swap_baseadaln looks like FastH3 and swap_fasth3adaln like the floor, FastH3's few-step ability lives in the backbone and gates despite their small norm, and the weight-space map misleads about function.
